brief: J.P. Morgan's Positioning Intelligence revisits the risks from its prior note (deteriorating long-short alpha, neutral CTAs, soft retail demand) and asks whether capitulation has occurred and whether hedge fund alpha or the market can rebound. It argues both could rebound near-term, with history favoring a rebound, but the path stays murky. Multi-Strat de-grossing was the largest 20-day event since Covid; long-short spreads turned positive Tuesday and Thursday, leaving 5-day alpha near flat. Historically, after 20-day gross flows fall below the 5th percentile, alpha is higher over the next 20 days in 9 of 10 cases, with flows recovering after about 10 days, except post-Covid. Broader de-grossing resembles 2022's midterm pattern, continuing into mid-month before recovering in December alongside a market sell-off and more shorting. Past 5-/20-day return drops below -2z preceded rebounds in all eight recent cases, though the 2020 and 2018 drawdowns kept falling. No broad capitulation signal has appeared yet; EMEA and China bought while North America and Japan sold and de-grossed sharply, and European short covering hit an extreme 3z level. Leverage and momentum/AI exposure have reset toward multi-year lows, with Semis the most net-sold and Defensives ex-Healthcare beginning to rebound.
